newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU to threaten Spain over mobile phone fee.
newsitem.headline: EU to threaten Spain over mobile phone fee.

text.p: The European Commission is threatening Spain with legal action unless it redresses breaches in competition regulations after it charged a fee for the award of a mobile phone licence.
"The Commission is tired of waiting (for the Spanish government to propose a solution)," a Commission official said on Friday.

The source added that European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert had instructed officials to draft a decision under article 90 of the European Union treaty urging Spain to act quickly or face legal action. The decision could come as soon as mid-November.

At issue is the payment by the Airtel consortium, which is led by U.S. company AirTouch Communications Inc, of a 85-billion-peseta fee for winning a licence to operate a second mobile phone system in Spain.
Partly state-owned telecoms operator Telefonica de Espana did not have to pay any fee when it was given the first mobile phone licence.
The same situation happened in Italy, Belgium, Austria and Ireland when granting a second mobile phone licence.
The Commission, which must ensure fair competition in the Union, cried foul each time and ruled that either the existing operator paid the same fee or that the newcomer was compensated.
Spanish Development Minister Rafael Arias Salgado told the Commission in July he was confident Airtel and Telefonica would reach a deal.
But industry and Commission sources told Reuters that a deal was nowhere in sight.
The Commission has used article 90 to ensure national monopolies or state-owned companies are not given preferential rights that would distort competition.
